s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness during a long-haul flight with a background of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells
Multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI
key_facts: 58-year-old woman
Developed right arm weakness 8 hours into a long-haul flight
Medical history includes Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Presented with dehydration
Blood film showed auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 119 mm/h
D-dimer was 24.7 nmol/L
Fibrinogen was 15.6 μmol/L
Renal function showed signs of dehydration
Elevated tumor markers
Procoagulant and vasculitic studies were negative
ECG and telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac chamber size and function
Brain MRI showed multiple small foci of restricted diffusion
Carotid ultrasound showed normal carotid and vertebral artery anatomy

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen, history of autoimmune disease

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated D-dimer, fibrinogen, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI, history of autoimmune disease

shortlist.label: Cold agglutinin disease
shortlist.why_kept: Auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells on blood film, history of Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic anaemia

shortlist.label: Primary antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen, history of autoimmune disease, and presence of thrombotic events

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with right arm weakness, elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen levels, and multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI, along with a history of autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, are consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome. The presence of auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells on blood film and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen levels, the absence of other typical findings such as thrombocytopenia and prolonged PT/INR makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: The patient's brain MRI shows multiple small foci of restricted diffusion, but the absence of other typical findings such as headache, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Cold agglutinin disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, the presence of auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells on blood film is not specific to cold agglutinin disease and can be seen in other conditions.

rejected.label: Primary antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: This diagnosis is similar to antiphospholipid syndrome, but the presence of other autoimmune conditions such as autoimmune haemolytic anaemia makes primary antiphospholipid syndrome less likely.
